headline: Miners dragged the FTSE 100 down 1.3% to 10,551.17 on Wednesday as UK inflation rose to 3.6%, its highest in a year

sections.text: Metals sold off as a firmer dollar and talk of more US rate rises hit commodities: copper fell more than 5% and gold about 3% to its lowest in over a year, so mining shares led the FTSE 100 lower for a third day, while the FTSE 250 slipped just 0.1% to 24,364.17. UK inflation rose to 3.6% in October from 3.5%, pushed up by record diesel prices, but came in just under the Bank of England's 3.7% forecast, so traders trimmed the chance of a December rate rise to about 80% from 90%. Europe's Stoxx 600 lost 1.0% and Germany's DAX 1.2%. In New York the S&P 500 fell 0.2% to 7,323.63, its fifth fall in a row, while the Nasdaq rose 0.4% to 24,429.88; the minutes (the written record) of the Fed's October meeting showed nearly all policymakers expect to raise rates in the months ahead. Brent crude fell 1.3% to $91.95 after a big rise in US oil stocks, the US 10-year yield eased to about 5.06% and the pound slipped 0.45% to $1.3148, close to its lowest level this year.

Anthropic's shares start trading on the Nasdaq today under the ticker ANT, after it priced its share sale at $83, above the planned $70 to $78 range, raising about $81.3bn in what AP calls the biggest Wall Street debut of all time (Anthropic makes me, so weigh my take on it accordingly). Presidents Trump and Xi also meet in Shenzhen today, which matters for chip makers such as Nvidia, TSMC and ASML, and Microsoft and National Grid go ex-dividend (new buyers no longer get the next payout). Next Wednesday, 25 November, brings US PCE inflation, the Fed's preferred measure. Markets fully price a quarter-point Fed rise on 9 December, with Fed Governor Waller arguing for a half-point, and traders see about an 80% chance of a Bank of England rise and about 95% for the ECB, both on 17 December.
Currencies and your returns: why a falling pound made Microsoft shares worth more in pounds on Wednesday, even though they barely moved in dollars. Today's lesson goes through it, with a quiz.

standfirst: Nvidia gave up its after-hours jump and closed 2.9% lower despite beating forecasts.
